chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya raised it to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who intends to eat the yoghurt and for it not to harm him, so let him pour the digestive over it. I said to him, 'And what is the digestive?' He said: 'Al-Nankhwah (a herb)'.

key_terms.النَّانْخَواهُ: Ankhwa, a specific herb known for its digestive properties
key_terms.الْمَاسْت: Mast, a type of thick yoghurt or fermented dairy product
key_terms.الْهَاضُوم: The digestive, a substance that aids in digestion

ai.seo_question: What herb should be added to yoghurt to aid digestion according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the integration of prophetic medicine (*al-Tibb al-Nabawi*) with Shia jurisprudence, where Imam Al-Hasan (AS) identifies *Nankhwah* (likely anise or fennel) as a digestive aid for *Mast* (fermented dairy). It highlights the practical application of herbal remedies in daily life, emphasizing the prevention of digestive discomfort through specific dietary combinations. This reflects the broader Shia scholarly tradition of valuing empirical health advice alongside spiritual teachings.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, 
(It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who intends to eat the yoghurt and for it not to harm him, so let him pour the digestive (الْهَاضُومَ) over it’. I said to himasws, ‘And what is the digestive?’ Heasws said: ‘Al-Nankhwah (A herb)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya in a marfu‘ manner has narrated the following: “Once abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘
If one wants to eat yogurt without harming him, he should pour al-Hadum on it.’ I then asked, ‘What is al-Hadum ?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is al- Nankhoxvah.’”
